A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same second-order interpretation of CLIP neurons. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuron-ablation experiments, sparse reconstruction evaluations, generated adversarial examples, concept discovery and segmentation results, including additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds ImageNet-R ablations and further qualitative neuron examples.

M1.justification: The second-order pathway, principal-component approximation, sparse text decomposition and application procedures are retained. Equation-index corrections align the mathematics with the existing source-neuron construction; they do not establish an algorithm change. Concept discovery is relocated intact.

E1.justification: v3 adds ImageNet-R evaluation of second-order effects in Figure 10, extending coverage beyond the original ImageNet domain. Existing classification, segmentation, concept-discovery and semantic-adversarial scenarios remain, including those in the appendices.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the Random, Indirect effect and Similar words baselines. Table 4 retains all seven segmentation comparators, including TextSpan. The added discussion of alternative concept-extraction approaches does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Corresponding ImageNet evaluations are described as using the test set in v1 and the validation set in v3. This revises the reported split, without establishing that experiments were rerun or images changed. The new ImageNet-R evaluation specifically tests ViT-B-32 layers 8–10.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 checks whether the ablation and reconstruction patterns persist on ImageNet-R. Figure 13 extends qualitative inspection to examples through rank 50, exposing concepts beyond the top-four descriptions. Existing ViT-L and first-order ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three repetitions of adversarial generation and report standard deviations in Table 3. v3 adds no new seed disclosures, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds ImageNet-R ablation curves and further ranked neuron-image examples. Existing numerical tables retain their values: dog-to-deer attack success remains 22.7 ± 0.5 images per 100 in Table 3, and segmentation pixel accuracy/mIoU/mAP remain 78.1/59.0/84.9 in Table 4.

T1.justification: Equations (5), (9) and (11) correct neuron activation/output-weight indices from the downstream layer l′ to the source layer l while retaining downstream attention indices. This is a localized mathematical correction to the stated construction; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and closing discussion narrow the highlighted applications from three to adversarial generation and segmentation. Concept discovery remains in Appendix A.5. The central claims about selective, approximately rank-one second-order effects and neuron polysemy are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds concrete failure modes involving language-model descriptions and omitted elements in generated images. Appendix A.5 acknowledges alternative concept-extraction approaches, and Figure 13 notes that top-four descriptions miss some activated concepts. These qualify the retained methods and interpretations.

D1.justification: Implementation choices, generation prompts, neuron-selection parameters and compute disclosures are retained, including one A100 GPU and the five-day ViT-L experiment. The project URL is unchanged; dropping 'and code' from its label does not establish a change in resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Shah et al. (2024) on modeling network computation and Hendrycks et al. (2021) for ImageNet-R. Appendix A.5 additionally relates concept discovery to the already-cited Bhalla et al. approach. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Concept discovery moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix A.5, and the application overview and discussion receive localized rewrites. Cross-references expand and citation/header styles change, but most exposition and the overall argument retain their earlier structure.

P2.justification: v3 substantially retypesets the document in ICLR format. Tables 3 and 4 change from side-by-side to wider stacked displays, segmentation examples become a larger standalone figure, and appendix displays are reorganized. New Figures 10 and 13 add a robustness plot and ranked-image montage.

improvement.justification: The ImageNet-R check and broader neuron examples modestly strengthen validation, while corrected layer indices and explicit generation-pipeline limitations improve precision and qualification. Core comparative results and statistical support remain unchanged, and concept-discovery evidence is preserved in the appendix.
